questions.q: What makes an automated check actually a 'quality gate' rather than just a dashboard, per this lesson?
options: It must run in under one minute
It must only check Apex code, never metadata
It has to be written in YAML
It is wired to a real consequence -- the pipeline or pull request genuinely cannot proceed past it on a failure
questions.explain: A check that reports a result nobody acts on is just a dashboard; what makes it a gate is that failure actually blocks progress.

questions.q: What repository setting actually gives a GitHub Actions check the power to block a pull request merge?
options: A branch protection rule requiring that specific check to pass before merging
A .gitignore entry
Setting --wait to 60 on the deploy command
Naming the workflow file ci.yml
questions.explain: Branch protection rules, configured under repository Settings, are what turn a failing check from a red X someone could ignore into something that actually disables the merge button.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say many teams set their CI coverage gate a few points above the platform's 75% production minimum?
options: Because 75% is not actually enforced by Salesforce at all
Because the CLI requires a minimum of 80% to even run
To catch a coverage regression early with some margin, rather than leaving zero room before a production deploy would outright fail on the platform's own rule
There is no reason given; it's an arbitrary convention
questions.explain: Setting the CI gate above the hard platform minimum gives a margin that surfaces a coverage regression before it would actually block a production deployment outright.

questions.q: Why does this lesson recommend a severity threshold on a static analysis gate rather than failing the build on every finding?
options: Static analysis tools cannot report severity at all
Severity thresholds are required by Salesforce platform rules
Thresholds have no real effect on team behavior
A gate that fails on every minor style nit trains a team to ignore it, defeating the point -- thresholds let low-severity findings get reported without blocking merges
questions.explain: Failing on trivial findings erodes trust in the gate; a severity threshold keeps the gate meaningful by blocking merge only on findings serious enough to matter.

questions.q: Which of these is specifically enforced by the Salesforce platform itself, not by a pipeline's own configuration?
options: The CI gate's chosen severity threshold for static analysis
The exact wording of a branch protection rule
The 75% minimum Apex code coverage requirement for a production deployment
The specific name given to a GitHub Actions job
questions.explain: The 75% coverage minimum is enforced by the Salesforce platform itself at deploy time, independent of any pipeline configuration -- a pipeline can only add a stricter check on top of it.
